2027-02-15.title: Second Monday of the Great Fast
2027-02-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-15.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-15.verse: there is nothing outside a person that by going in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile.
theo: The second week of the Great Fast opens with a Gospel that seems, at first hearing, to argue against fasting. Jesus calls the crowd and says: “Listen to me, all of you, and understand: there is nothing outside a person that by going in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile.” Mark even adds his own comment: “Thus he declared all foods clean.” Older members of many St Thomas Christian families remember a Great Fast kept without meat, fish, eggs or milk, and some households still keep it so; in earlier generations many took only one full meal a day. Why, then, do we give up food that Jesus himself called clean? Not because the fish curry is unclean. We fast because the stomach is a good teacher of the heart. The one who learns to say no to a plate learns, little by little, to say no to the anger, the envy and the greed that come out of the heart. The Church fasts from clean things in order to become clean within.

Jesus names what really defiles. “For it is from within, from the human heart, that evil intentions come: fornication, theft, murder, adultery, avarice, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, envy, slander, pride, folly. All these evil things come from within, and they defile a person.” It is an uncomfortable list, and it is honest. Nobody needs to be taught envy or pride; they grow in the heart like weeds in a compound left alone for one monsoon. The wise of Israel said: “Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.” A fast that watches the kitchen but not the heart has guarded the wrong door. That is why many of our elders spoke of fasting with the tongue too: no gossip, no cursing, no sharp word at the dinner table, for as long as the fast lasts.

Paul's letter to Titus gives the other half of the answer. We cannot clean the heart by our own scrubbing. Paul describes believers as they once were, “foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to various passions and pleasures, passing our days in malice and envy.” “But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.” The heart is washed in baptism and renewed by the Spirit poured out “richly”. Fasting does not buy this grace; it makes room for it. So Paul can ask for a very ordinary holiness, the kind that shows in a neighbourhood: “to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show every courtesy to everyone.” This week, let the fast reach the heart, and let the heart reach the street.
outline: Ask: if Jesus declared all foods clean, why do we still fast?
The stomach as a teacher of the heart.
The list of what really defiles.
God's kindness appeared; the Spirit poured out richly.
Speak evil of no one, be gentle with everyone.
“there is nothing outside a person that by going in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile.”
live: For the rest of this week, speak evil of no one, not even in jest; if you slip, say a short prayer for the person you spoke about.
Each night before sleep, look back on the day and ask which of Jesus' list came out of your heart today.
Find out the date of your baptism and thank God for it in your family prayer.
2027-02-15.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you see the heart and you know what comes out of it. Let our fasting from food become a fasting from envy, slander and pride. By the water of rebirth you have washed us; pour out your Spirit on us richly again, so that our words may be gentle and our hearts clean. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we ask to approach the holy mysteries with a clean heart; the Lord who washed us in baptism feeds us now, so that what comes out of us may be his goodness.

quick: We fast from clean food so that the heart may become clean.
What defiles comes from within; guard the heart.
God saved us by his mercy, through the water of rebirth and the Spirit.
2027-02-15.action: Speak evil of no one today, and say one kind word about someone you usually criticise.
2027-02-15.question: What comes out of my heart when I am tired or hurt?

family.explain: Jesus says that dirt on our hands or food in our stomach does not make us bad. What makes us bad comes from inside: angry thoughts, lies, jealousy, unkind words. During the Great Fast we give up some food, but we also ask Jesus to clean our hearts.
family.intention: We pray that our home may be free of unkind words this week.
family.ask: Ask: “Which unkind word shall we all try not to say at home this week?”

illus: A grandmother near Thrissur was known in her parish for the strictness of her Lenten fast: no fish, no eggs, no milk in her tea for fifty days. One Lent her granddaughter, home from college, asked her gently why she still complained about the daughter-in-law every evening. The old woman was silent for a long time. That year she added one more thing to her fast: no complaint about anyone at the dinner table. Her son said later that it was the hardest fast she ever kept, and the first one the whole house noticed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you look into our hearts. Clean them by your Spirit as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Nothing outside a person can defile (Mark 7:15). What does my fast this year really aim at?
From within, from the human heart (Mark 7:21). Which of the things Jesus lists do I struggle with most?
Speak evil of no one (Titus 3:2). Where does my tongue most need a fast?
pm.resp: Lord, create in us a clean heart.
interc: For the Church, that her fasting may bear the fruit of clean hearts.
For families where harsh words have become a habit.
For those who are victims of slander and gossip.
For the newly baptised and for catechumens.
For our group, that our words may build one another up.
pm.close: Father, by the goodness and loving kindness of our Saviour you have washed us and renewed us. Keep our hearts clean, our tongues gentle and our fast sincere. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today Jesus says something surprising in the middle of our fast: nothing outside a person that goes in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile (Mark 7:15). Mark tells us that in this way Jesus declared all foods clean.
So why do we still give up fish and meat? Not because they are unclean. We give up good things so that our hearts learn to say no. The stomach becomes a teacher of the heart.

Jesus then names what really makes us unclean: evil intentions, theft, deceit, envy, slander, pride (Mark 7:21–22). These come from within. A fast that guards the kitchen but not the heart has guarded the wrong door.

And we cannot clean our hearts by ourselves. Saint Paul says that God saved us not because of our works but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). Let us ask him this week to keep our tongues gentle, to speak evil of no one, and to show every courtesy to everyone. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says that what makes us bad is not the food we eat but the unkind things that come out of our hearts and mouths. This week, can you fast from one unkind word?
